content.text:
# Live LLM testing: the deterministic gate and the supervised benches

gh-1199 — the merge-blocking Quality gate answers exactly one question:
**did this PR break the code?** It runs exclusively on mock LLMs
(`MockLlmServer` and friends), so a model's mood, drift, or rate limit can
never red a merge. Real-model verification answers a different question —
**does the agent work against real models today?** — and it lives in the
bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run **under
supervision**, never in the PR path.

## The `llm` tag boundary

A test that performs live provider I/O carries `@Tags(['integration',
'llm'])`. Everything integration-tagged without `llm` is mock by
construction and runs in the deterministic gate.

| Where | Live (`llm`) tests | Mock (gate) tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| per-PR integration shards (`pty-integration-linux`) | excluded — `shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm` at selection, `--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm` at invocation | run |
| `integration-mock` leg (no-key) | excluded (`--exclude-tags llm,...`) | run |
| tag-only provider-smoke job (`v*` tags) | run, with secrets | — |
| `nightly.yml` | run, with secrets (supervised, unsharded) | run |
| bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS) | run under supervision | — |
| your machine (debugging) | `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` | `dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags llm` |

gh-1538: `nightly.yml` is builds + integration-only — the unit shards,
analyze, coverage and CRAP/jscpd gates run exclusively in the pre-merge SM
validation gate (#1537); nightly keeps the release build matrix plus these
integration suites.

The boundary is enforced, not aspirational:

- `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step on every PR, plus
  `test/scripts/llm_tag_boundary_test.dart` in the regular suite) fails
  when an integration-tagged file looks live — a real provider URL, or a
  credential-key literal with no mock/loopback marker — without the `llm`
  tag. A PR that legitimately adds a live test is blocked until tagged;
  genuinely deterministic files that trip the heuristic are pinned in the
  script's `AUDIT_MOCK` audit list with a justification (reviewed in the
  PR). New live tests can never silently join the gate again.
- `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` is the AC1 red/green
  proof: it runs the exact CI shard-selection invocation and asserts no
  live file is emitted — and that without `--exclude-tag llm` one would
  be.
- `llm`-tagged files stay in the `dart analyze` scope of every PR (they
  are excluded from RUN, never from compile — no dead-code rot), and
  nightly compiles and runs them with secrets.

## Mock-script hygiene (gh-1171)

Scripted mocks serve a fixed queue; incidental LLM traffic (memory
auto-tagging, title/summary calls) used to exhaust it and 500-storm the
test. The contract since gh-1171:

- content-route the scripted conversation on unique markers — background
  noise can then never pop a scripted response;
- pin known noise to a **sticky wildcard** scenario (`sticky: true` +
  `match: "Existing tags:"`) so an extra call re-serves the last response
  forever instead of exhausting into a 500;
- keep the conversation scenarios strict — a matched-but-dry scenario must
  still fail loudly, or a real loop regression goes unnoticed.
  `test/integration/memory_taggen_script_pin_test.dart` REG-pins the
  memory leg's wildcard.

## Flake quarantine (gh-1199 AC6)

A test red in **≥2 distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h** is a proven flake
(the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run is
a regression). `.github/workflows/flake-watch.yml` (hourly,
`scripts/flake_watch.py`) then:

1. creates/updates a `flake`-labelled issue carrying the failing run links
   and SHAs (E3: the quarantine never swallows a real regression — the
   evidence is attached), and
2. opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
   `scripts/test_quarantine.json`.

The gate legs pipe their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, so
a quarantined file leaves the deterministic gate until its fix PR lands.
Granularity is the file (dart test cannot exclude one test inside a file);
the entry's `test` field records the offending test. **Nightly
deliberately does NOT apply the quarantine** — the file keeps running
supervised, producing the 10/10-style repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC4) the
un-quarantine PR must cite.

## What is NOT here

No live runs in any scheduled PR-path job; no bench-harness changes (they
already run supervised); no reduction in mock coverage — the mock suites
keep every assertion the live ones make, minus the network.

if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'pubdev')
    outputs:
      status: ${{ steps.check.outputs.status }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pubspec }}
      published_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.published }}
      run_url: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'pubdev'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=pubdev) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing published"
          exit 1

      # gh-1561: the never-triggered self-heal re-pushes the latest tag with
      # the fa-release-bot App token — a GITHUB_TOKEN push can never cascade
      # (gh-1172), the App's push can (the same mechanism ci.yml's release
      # job uses to cut tags). Job-scoped, expires with the job; this job's
      # own GITHUB_TOKEN stays read-scoped (job-level permissions block).
      # Shape mirrors the validator-proven precedent (ci.yml release job,
      # the create-github-app-token step): NO `if:` at all — secrets
      # context in a step-if trips GitHub's workflow validator; and a mint
      # on an unconfigured App (forks, rotation gap) fails, is SWALLOWED by
      # continue-on-error, outputs.token stays empty, and the script's
      # manual-re-push alarm fires exactly as before this change.
      # Least privilege, verified against the PINNED action (v3.2.0,
      # bcd2ba49 — review thread 10): the composite `permissions` input
      # does NOT exist there (action.yml defines only the generated
      # `permission-*` inputs — GitHub warns `Unexpected input(s)
      # 'permissions'` and the action never reads it; ci.yml:3980 rides
      # that warning). The HONORED ceiling is the granular
      # `permission-contents` input, which the action turns into the mint
      # request's permissions map: contents:write only — the tag re-push —
      # instead of the installation's full grant set. Without it the token
      # inherits every permission the fa-release-bot installation has.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        id: app-token
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          permission-contents: write

      - name: Verify pub.dev serves the pubspec version
        id: check
        # gh-1192: the classification (up-to-date / release-in-flight /
        # recovered + the unchanged alarms) lives in the extracted script so
        # it is shell-harness testable (test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
        # RELEASE_APP_TOKEN is empty when the mint above skipped (App not
        # configured) — the script then fails over to the manual-re-push
        # alarm instead of attempting a re-arm.
        env:
          RELEASE_APP_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh

  # ── Release-draft sweeper (issue #282) ────────────────────────────────────
  # Hygiene leg: no pipeline step may leave a draft release behind (the
  # 3-week-old v0.1.190 rot). The per-job guards in build-macos/build-mobile
  # own the failure path; this sweeper is the daily backstop — anything that
  # slips through (a cancelled run, a path without a guard) is deleted after
  # 24h and a deduplicated self-closing issue names the creating run so a
  # RECURRING stuck draft points at its broken step instead of rotting.
  # Runs on every daily (and manual) invocation regardless of leg results —
  # change-gating must not gate hygiene.
  sweep-drafts:
    name: Sweep stale release drafts
    needs: plan
    if: always() # even when plan failed or all legs skipped
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete draft releases
      actions: read # name each swept draft's creating run (gh run list 403s without it, review of #294)
      issues: write # deduplicated self-closing sweep issue
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Delete drafts older than 24h and file the dedup issue
        run: bash scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh

  # ── Report + self-healing issues ─────────────────────────────────────────
  report:
    name: Summary + self-filed issues
    needs: [plan, testflight, play, pubdev, cli, website, addin]
    if: always() # runs even when plan failed, so plan failures enter the self-healing loop too
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      issues: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Job summary table and issue lifecycle
        env:
          NEXT_TAG: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
          PLAN_RESULT: ${{ needs.plan.result }}
          DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE: ai-teammate
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT: ${{ needs.testflight.result }}
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT_URL: ${{ needs.testflight.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PLAY: ${{ needs.play.result }}
          LEG_PLAY_URL: ${{ needs.play.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PUBDEV: ${{ needs.pubdev.result }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_STATUS: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.status }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBSPEC: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.pubspec_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBLISHED: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.published_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_URL: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_CLI: ${{ needs.cli.result }}
          LEG_CLI_URL: ${{ needs.cli.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_WEBSITE: ${{ needs.website.result }}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify pub.dev serves the LATEST TAG version — the daily-publish pubdev
# leg's check (gh-1192, reworked gh-1522). Extracted verbatim from the
# inline step in daily-publish.yml so the classification is shell-harness
# testable (fake gh/curl fixtures, test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
#
# gh-1522: the git tag is the single source of truth — the committed
# pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder, so the version under test is
# the LATEST REMOTE TAG (git ls-remote), never a file read. The retired
# bump-commit flow's «tag not cut yet / bump on main» states are gone:
# the version IS a tag that exists on the remote by construction, so the
# appear-wait branch is deleted as impossible.
#
# The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
# accepts OIDC only from tag-push runs — the release-event twin of a tag can
# never publish, #1368). This script VERIFIES pub.dev serves the tag
# version and, when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push
# publish run — a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims.
# Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an issue with a
# manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
#
# States (gh-1192; refined by #1368 — the 2026-10-07 false alarm; gh-1522):
#   up-to-date          pub.dev already serves the latest tag version
#   release-in-flight   the publish outcome is NOT yet observable — neutral
#                       skip (no ::error::, no auto-filed issue); the next
#                       scheduled daily re-verifies. Covers:
#                         · tag exists but its ci.yml run is not visible yet
#                           and the tag is younger than the grace window
#                         · the tag's PUSH ci.yml run is queued/in_progress —
#                           the script waits up to RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS for
#                           a terminal state first (Never-again: the leg
#                           waits for the publish conclusion, with a
#                           timeout); past the budget the outcome stays
#                           unobserved and the skip stays neutral — runner
#                           starvation may hold a queued run for hours
#   recovered           the failed tag-push publish run was re-run and
#                       pub.dev caught up
#   private             publish_to: none — nothing to verify
# Alarms — each error says WHICH state (Never-again #2):
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version
#
# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag
# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
# run, never the stale tag age, and a completed fresh run verifies normally.
#
# gh-1561: the never-triggered arms first try to RE-ARM — the tag is
# force-re-pushed (SAME commit, fresh annotated tag object: a new tag-push
# event the leg could not otherwise produce) with the fa-release-bot App

# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The daily-publish `pubdev` leg (run 42964867375) failed: pub.dev kept serving 1.0.701 while the latest tag was v1.0.706, and the leg's rerun-recovery could not make the publish happen ("publish did not upload; manual publish needed").

**Root cause**: The tag-push CI run for v1.0.706 (run 42898188002) never published because its hard gate `integration` — "Provider smoke (LLM, tag-only)" (`dart test --tags "integration && llm"`) — went red: all 4 live tests in `test/integration/provider_ollama_test.dart` failed against the real Ollama Cloud API with `402 Payment Required` ("Add usage credits or subscribe…"). At v1.0.706 the Ollama suite's skip gate was key-presence-only (`final _skip = (_apiKey?.isEmpty ?? true) ? 'OLLAMA_API_KEY not set' : false;`), and `OLLAMA_API_KEY` is the one provider secret actually configured in the CI environment — so the paid-provider suite RAN in CI, and the credit-exhausted Ollama account (not any product regression) reddened the smoke. `publish` requires `needs.integration.result == 'success'` (`ci.yml`, `publish` job `if:`), so 1.0.706 was never uploaded; the daily leg's `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh` then classified the tag as behind, re-ran the failed publish run (`gh run rerun --failed`), the same smoke failed again, and the leg errored out.

Failure evidence (Provider smoke log, v1.0.706 run, job 130340312108 attempt 2):
- `❌ provider_ollama_test.dart: … streams reasoning + text deltas …` — `Expected: <Instance of 'StartEvent'> / Actual: <Instance of 'ErrorEvent'>`
- `❌ provider_ollama_test.dart: … drives one full tool round-trip …` — `Actual: '402: {"error":{"message":"Add usage credits or subscribe and save up to 66%: https://ollama.com/plans …","type":"api_error",…}}'`
- `##[error]2 tests passed, 4 failed, 21 skipped.` — all 21 skips say "not set" for their keys; ANTHROPIC/GOOGLE/OPENROUTER keys are absent from CI, only `OLLAMA_API_KEY` is configured.

**Impact**: A third-party billing state (Ollama Cloud credits) blocked the whole release train: v1.0.706 (and the window around it) never reached pub.dev, and the daily pubdev leg self-filed this issue. No product code was broken.

**Fix approach**: Live paid-provider suites must never gate the publish on upstream billing/quota. This is the "2026-11-10 nightly policy": every `integration && llm` live suite gets an explicit opt-in env flag (`FA_OLLAMA_LIVE=1`, `FA_ANTHROPIC_LIVE=1`, `FA_GOOGLE_LIVE=1`, `FA_OPENROUTER_LIVE=1`, `FA_GLM_LIVE=1`, `FA_COPILOT_LIVE=1`, `FA_CHATGPT_CODEX_LIVE=1`, `FA_CODEX_BOOT_LIVE=1`) so CI smoke runs stay green (skip) unless a human opts in. The change is already merged.

**Already fixed**: PR #2092 (commit `b9eba2a`, tagged v1.0.707) added the opt-in gates to all eight live provider suites (`test/integration/provider_{ollama,anthropic,google,openrouter,glm,copilot,chatgpt_codex,codex_boot}*_test.dart`). The v1.0.707 tag run's Provider smoke passed (`🎉 1 test passed, 26 skipped.`, job 130351338662), its `Publish to pub.dev` job succeeded, and pub.dev now serves **1.0.707** (latest remote tag = v1.0.707). The next daily `pubdev` leg classifies `up-to-date` → green → this issue auto-closes.

**Verification**: reproduction = the exact CI invocation `OLLAMA_API_KEY=<present> dart test --tags "integration && llm"` on the current tree — the Ollama suite skips ("live Ollama Cloud is opt-in; set FA_OLLAMA_LIVE=1 to run") and the suite is green, matching the v1.0.707 CI outcome. Run locally; see outputs/response.md.

### Root Cause
The daily-publish `pubdev` leg failed because the v1.0.706 tag-push run never published: its hard gate "Provider smoke (LLM, tag-only)" ran the live Ollama Cloud suite (`test/integration/provider_ollama_test.dart`) — `OLLAMA_API_KEY` is the one provider secret configured in CI and the suite was gated only on key presence — and the credit-exhausted Ollama account answered `402 Payment Required` on all 4 tests ("Add usage credits or subscribe…"). The smoke went red (`2 tests passed, 4 failed, 21 skipped`), `publish` requires `needs.integration.result == 'success'`, so pub.dev stayed at 1.0.701; the leg's rerun-recovery re-ran the failed run, the same smoke failed again, and the leg errored ("publish did not upload"). A third-party billing state, not a product regression, blocked the release train.

### Fix
Already fixed by PR #2092 (commit `b9eba2a`, tagged v1.0.707): all eight live provider suites got explicit opt-in gates (`FA_OLLAMA_LIVE=1`, `FA_ANTHROPIC_LIVE=1`, `FA_GOOGLE_LIVE=1`, `FA_OPENROUTER_LIVE=1`, `FA_GLM_LIVE=1`, `FA_COPILOT_LIVE=1`, `FA_CHATGPT_CODEX_LIVE=1`, `FA_CODEX_BOOT_LIVE=1`) — CI smoke never runs paid providers without a human opt-in. No further code change needed; no PR opened.

### Test Coverage
- Reproduced CI conditions locally on the current tree: `OLLAMA_API_KEY=<set> dart test --tags "integration && llm"` → exit 0, `1 test passed, 26 skipped`; the 4 formerly-failing Ollama tests skip with "live Ollama Cloud is opt-in; set FA_OLLAMA_LIVE=1 to run".
- CI evidence: v1.0.706 smoke failed (4× ollama 402, job 130340312108); v1.0.707 smoke passed (`1 test passed, 26 skipped`, job 130351338662) and its `Publish to pub.dev` succeeded — pub.dev now serves 1.0.707, equal to the latest remote tag v1.0.707, so the next daily `pubdev` leg classifies `up-to-date` → green → this issue auto-closes.

### Notes
- Root cause of the red was upstream billing (Ollama Cloud 402), not harness code; the 2026-11-10 opt-in policy in PR #2092 is the durable fix.
- With the opt-in policy the CI provider smoke exercises no live provider by design (mock parity lives in the unit suites; live runs stay opt-in/nightly-supervised per docs/live-llm-testing.md).
- v1.0.707's run still shows `Build iOS (debug, unsigned)` red (self-hosted `macos-m5` platform leg) — platform-class only, it never gates `dart_ok`/publish (verified: publish uploaded 1.0.707).

content.text:
All verification complete. The full picture:

**What happened:** The daily-publish `pubdev` leg failed because the v1.0.706 tag-push run never published. Its hard gate — the "Provider smoke (LLM, tag-only)" job — ran the live Ollama Cloud suite (`OLLAMA_API_KEY` is the only provider secret configured in CI, and at v1.0.706 that suite was gated on key-presence only), and the credit-exhausted Ollama account answered `402 Payment Required` on all 4 tests → smoke red → `publish` gated off → pub.dev stuck at 1.0.701. The leg's rerun-recovery re-ran the failed run; the same smoke failed again; the leg errored "publish did not upload".

**Resolution:** Already fixed on the current base by PR #2092 (`b9eba2a`, tagged v1.0.707), which added explicit opt-in gates (`FA_OLLAMA_LIVE=1`, `FA_ANTHROPIC_LIVE=1`, …) to all eight live provider suites. Evidence: v1.0.707's smoke passed (`1 test passed, 26 skipped`, job 130351338662), its publish job uploaded 1.0.707, pub.dev now serves 1.0.707 = latest remote tag → the next daily `pubdev` leg classifies `up-to-date` → green → gh-2108 auto-closes. Reproduced the exact CI conditions locally: `OLLAMA_API_KEY=<set> dart test --tags "integration && llm"` → exit 0, `1 test passed, 26 skipped`. No code change needed, no PR.

Artifacts written: `outputs/rca.md`, `outputs/already_fixed.json`, `outputs/response.md`.

**Bug already fixed** — commit `b9eba2a` (PR #2092, tag v1.0.707): live provider suites are now opt-in (`FA_*_LIVE=1`), so upstream billing state can no longer redden the Provider smoke and hold the publish hostage. The release train recovered (1.0.707 published); this issue auto-closes when the leg's next daily run verifies `up-to-date`.
